title: Shirshasana
notes: Also known as Kapalasana or Viparita Karani.

sequence.action: While coming from the 6th to the 7th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara, sit on the knees, lock the fingers together, and place the elbows on the floor.
Doing rechaka and then puraka, place the crown of the head on the floor, interlocked hands cupping the back of the head.

Doing rechaka and puraka again, straighten the legs and, keeping them together and straight, lift them up with the power of the arms, tighten the body, point the toes, and keep the body erect using the strength of the arms. Stay, doing rechaka and puraka slowly and as many times as possible.
Doing rechaka slowly, bring the feet back down onto the floor, rest with the buttocks on the heels and the head on the floor for two minutes.
Doing puraka and then rechaka, jump back into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara.
The next vinyasas are as those described above.

while_holding: Draw the lower abdomen and the anus in fully and hold them tightly — mula bandha.
Do rechaka and puraka deeply, without kumbhaka.
Begin by staying five minutes, then ten, then fifteen, increasing the time in the state by five-minute increments over many days, months, and years, until able to stay for a full three hours.
benefits: Through the practice of Shirshasana, the subtle nadis of the head—that is, those related to the brain and sense organs, such as the eyes—are purified by an inflow of warm blood, and the power of memory is increased.
Eye disease is destroyed, the eyes glow, and long-sightedness improves.
The five sense organs, too, become purified.
cautions: Pregnant women should not practice this asana.
Aspirants should note that merely putting the head down and legs up, and then standing upside down is not Shirshasana; very simply, this is wrong.
For example, the entire body must stand upside down on the strength of the arms alone.
Hence, aspirants should never practice Shirshasana first.
Moreover, following Shirshasana, they should only sit in Padmasana and do pranayama and the like, but no further asanas.

verses.translation: We can dwell in (Shirshasana) for three hours.
verses.source: A scriptural saying, as quoted by Guruji

verses.sanskrit: Maranam bindu patena / Jivanam bindu dharanat / Tasmat sarvaprayatnena / Bindu dharanam abhyaset
verses.translation: Loss of bindu is death / and the preservation of it, life / So, by all means / is the holding of bindu to be preserved.
verses.source: The yoga shastra, as quoted by Guruji

verses.sanskrit: Yuva vrddho’tivrddho va vyadito durbalo’pi va / Abhyasat siddhim apnoti / Sarvayogeshvatandritah
verses.translation: Whether young or old, or very old / sick or debilitated / one who is vigilant attains, by means of practice, success in all the yogas.
